coordinates.note: Centroid of the OSM boundary of the whole site (bounding box roughly 40 km across), not any reactor building. Geocoder, so campus-grade only (A17); no fetched source gives coordinates for a Hanford reactor area.

name: Hanford Site
notes: The point is the centroid of the OpenStreetMap boundary of the whole site, so it can lie tens of kilometres from the reactor at which the 1953 detector stood; that reactor is not named in the sources read.

summary.plain: The Hanford Site, a very large U.S. Department of Energy reservation in southeastern Washington on the Columbia River, where Cowan and Reines made their first attempt to detect the neutrino in 1953.
summary.technical: Whole-site point for the Hanford Site (Benton County, Washington), the Manhattan Project plutonium-production site with nine reactors along the Columbia River. The 1953 Cowan-Reines detector stood at one of its reactors, which is not separately geolocated by any source read.
